title: Caedmon's Hymn — Lines 1–5
subtitle: Nū sculon herigean heofonrīces Weard...
objectives: Read and translate authentic Old English poetry and prose.

sections.heading: Content
sections.body:
Nū sculon herigean heofonrīces Weard,
Metodes meahte and his mōdgeþanc,
weorc Wuldorfæder, swā hē wundra gehwæs,
ēce Drihten, ōr onstealde.

Translation: 'Now we must praise the Guardian of the heavenly kingdom, the might of the Creator and his thought, the work of the Father of glory, as he, eternal Lord, established the beginning of every wonder.'

This is the first half of Caedmon's Hymn, the oldest surviving Old English poem (c. 658–680 CE). Nine lines total.
